newsitem.title: USA: Noriega writing his memoirs as 'America's Prisoner'.
newsitem.headline: Noriega writing his memoirs as 'America's Prisoner'.

text.p: Manuel Antonio Noriega has played half a dozen roles on the world stage during his long and notorious career as a political figure.

Next year, the deposed Panamanian dictator, former CIA informant, convicted drug-trafficking racketeer and born-again Christian will add yet another job title to his repertoire when he becomes a published author.

"The Memoirs of Manuel Noriega: America's Prisoner" is the working title for his new book, which is expected to appear in U.S. bookstores next March with a price tag of $25, according to his New York publisher, Random House Inc.
The 336-page volume is co-authored by the one-time military leader and American journalist Peter Eisner, who served both as foreign editor and Latin American correspondent for Newsday.

Early promotional material bills Noriega as "the only prisoner of war in the United States" and promises revelations about world political celebrities ranging from former Presidents George Bush and Jimmy Carter to Cuban dictator Fidel Castro and Libyan President Muammar Gaddafi.

Noriega, who was captured during the 1989 U.S. invasion of Panama, is now serving a 40-year prison sentence for his 1992 conviction on drug and racketeering charges. The 11th U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals in Atlanta heard oral arguments on his appeal and motion for a new trial on Wednesday.
Eisner says the memoirs will be presented as first-person narrative that Noriega taped in his federal prison cell in Florida over the course of three years.
